title: Is AliExpress Available in Pakistan? (2026)
summary: Is AliExpress available in Pakistan? Yes, it ships here - but payment is card-only, delivery takes weeks and duty is charged at the door.
body_markdown:
Yes. AliExpress is available in Pakistan. The website and the app both open here, Pakistan is a selectable delivery country, most sellers ship to Pakistani addresses, and orders do arrive. What is not available is the part most shoppers here care about: there is no cash on delivery, the wait runs into weeks rather than days, you need a card that clears an international payment, and duty can be collected at your door. So "available" is true for ordering and false for convenience. Below: what works from Pakistan, what quietly fails, how to check a listing before you pay, and the cash-on-delivery route to the same Chinese factories if the prepaid wait is the part you would rather skip.


## What "available" actually means, point by point


People ask this question for six different reasons. Here is each one answered separately, because the answer is not the same for all of them.


- **The site and the app** — both load in Pakistan. You can register with a Pakistani mobile number or an email address and browse the full catalogue in English.
- **Shipping** — Pakistan appears in the delivery-country list. Most listings ship here; a minority do not, and that is set per seller, not per country.
- **Payment** — prepaid only. A debit or credit card that is enabled for international transactions, or a supported wallet. Rupees in cash at the door is not an option.
- **Delivery** — plan in weeks. The window depends on the shipping method you choose at checkout, and free or economy shipping is the slowest of them.
- **Customs** — a cross-border parcel can be assessed on arrival. The courier normally collects whatever is due before handing it over.
- **Returns** — the return address is in China and the postage is yours. For a low-value item, most buyers write it off instead.


None of that makes AliExpress a bad platform. It makes it a platform built for markets where card payment is normal and cross-border parcels are routine. Pakistan is neither, which is why the rest of[online shopping in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/cheapest-online-shopping-in-pakistan) looks so different — cash at the door, delivery measured in days, and a seller you can message in Urdu.


## Is AliExpress blocked in Pakistan?


No. There is no country block on AliExpress from Pakistan, and you do not need a VPN to shop there. If a page will not load or the app keeps spinning, the usual causes are an unstable connection, an app version that needs updating, or a browser extension interfering with the checkout script.


One warning about VPNs: shopping through one while paying with a Pakistani card is a good way to get the payment declined. Banks and payment processors read a mismatch between the card's country and the connection's country as a fraud signal. If you use a VPN for other things, turn it off before you pay.


## Does AliExpress ship to Pakistan?


Usually yes, but it is decided listing by listing. Two things to do before you get attached to a product:


1. **Set your delivery country to Pakistan first.** Do it in the header of the site or in the app settings, before you browse. Prices, shipping cost and the estimated window all change once the destination is set, and a shipping figure you saw before setting it means nothing.
2. **Read the shipping line on the product page.** It names the shipping method, the cost to Pakistan and an estimated delivery window. If the listing does not ship to Pakistan, that line will say so instead — which is your cue to find the same product from a different seller rather than to order anyway.


Sellers also exclude categories rather than countries sometimes. Items with batteries, liquids, powders and aerosols are the common ones, because they are restricted air cargo. If a listing that clearly ships to Pakistan suddenly refuses at checkout, the item's category is the first thing to suspect.


## Paying from Pakistan: what works and what fails


This is where most first orders die, and it is almost never AliExpress's fault.


**Your card is probably domestic-only until you say otherwise.** Many Pakistani debit cards ship with international transactions switched off. You enable them in your bank's app, in internet banking, or by calling the helpline — some banks let you switch them on for a limited window, which is a sensible way to do it.


**Expect an OTP step.** The payment goes through your bank's verification, so the phone registered with the bank has to be reachable at that moment. A failed OTP shows up as a generic decline on the checkout page, which is why "my card does not work on AliExpress" is usually "my card was never turned on for this".


**You are paying in a foreign currency.** Your bank converts at its own rate and may add a fee for a cross-border transaction. The rupee figure on your statement will not match the sticker price you saw, and that gap is part of the true cost of the order.


**Never move the payment off the platform.** If a seller asks you to pay by bank transfer, a wallet or a payment link instead of AliExpress checkout, stop. Off-platform payment removes every protection you have. We cover the trust side of this in more detail in[is AliExpress legit and safe to use in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/is-aliexpress-legit-safe-to-use-in-pakistan) .


## Writing a Pakistani address AliExpress can actually deliver to


The address form was designed for countries with reliable postcodes, and Pakistani addresses do not fit it neatly. Fill it like this:


- **Address line 1** — house or flat number, street name or number.
- **Address line 2** — block or sector, phase, colony or society name, plus a landmark. Couriers here navigate by landmark, not by postcode.
- **City and province** — the actual delivery city, not the nearest big one.
- **Postal code** — the five-digit code for your area. If you are unsure, your area's post office code is fine; the courier's last mile does not depend on it.
- **Phone** — a mobile number in the +92 format, and one you will answer. A cross-border courier that cannot reach you holds the parcel.
- **Name** — the name on your CNIC. If the parcel is held for clearance, a name mismatch turns a phone call into a trip to the courier's office.


## Shipping methods and how long the wait really is


AliExpress lists several shipping options per item, and the gap between the cheapest and the fastest is the whole story. Free or economy shipping is the slowest lane, with tracking that goes quiet for long stretches while the parcel moves by sea or waits for consolidation. Paid courier options cost more, move faster and track properly.


Whichever you pick, treat the estimate on the checkout page as a hope rather than a promise: a cross-border order passes through the seller's dispatch, the export hub, the flight or sailing, Pakistani clearance and only then the local courier. Any one of those can add days. For the stage-by-stage version of that journey — and what normally causes the delays — read[how long China-to-Pakistan delivery takes](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/china-to-pakistan-delivery-time) .


The practical rule: if you need the item for a wedding, a birthday or a deadline, do not order it from AliExpress. Buy that one locally and save the cross-border order for things you are not waiting on.


## Customs and duty: the part that surprises people


An AliExpress parcel is an import. It can be assessed for duty and taxes when it lands, and the courier usually collects that amount from you before delivery. The figure is based on what customs assesses the goods at, not always on what you paid, and the category the item falls under matters as much as its value.


Two things follow from that. First, the sticker price is not the landed price — add shipping, the currency conversion, and whatever is collected at the door before you compare it to a local seller. Second, do not ask a seller to declare a lower value. If the parcel is assessed on the real value anyway, you pay the difference plus the delay, and you have no standing in a dispute over an item you declared as a gift. The mechanics are laid out in[AliExpress customs and duty in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/aliexpress-customs-duty-in-pakistan-what-you-actually-pay) .


## Returns, refunds and disputes from Pakistan


AliExpress runs a buyer-protection window that is shown on your order page, and a dispute has to be opened inside it. Some habits that make disputes go your way:


- Do not press "confirm receipt" until you have opened the parcel and checked the item. Confirming ends the protection window early.
- Film the unboxing for anything expensive or fragile. A single photo of a broken item is weaker evidence than a clip that shows the sealed parcel first.
- Raise the dispute on the platform, not in the seller's chat. A friendly chat is not a record.
- Check the postage before you agree to return anything. Sending an item back to China often costs more than the item, which is why a partial refund is frequently the better deal.


## So what is not available in Pakistan?


This is the honest list, and it is the reason the question gets asked at all:


- Cash on delivery.
- Delivery in days.
- A return address inside Pakistan.
- Support in Urdu, in your timezone.
- A single rupee price that already includes shipping and duty.


If those five are what you were hoping for, you are not really looking for AliExpress. You are looking for China's prices with Pakistan's shopping habits attached.

Resellers ask the availability question with more at stake, because a delivery window that slips by two weeks is a customer who cancels. Prepaid cross-border sourcing also ties up your cash for the whole of that window, before you know whether the product sells.

## A checklist before you press order


1. Delivery country set to Pakistan before browsing.
2. The listing's shipping line confirms it ships here, with a cost and a window.
3. Card enabled for international transactions, phone in hand for the OTP.
4. VPN off.
5. Address written with a landmark, a reachable +92 number, and your CNIC name.
6. Landed cost estimated: item, shipping, conversion, likely duty.
7. Seller checked — rating, order count, and reviews with buyer photos.
8. Nothing ordered that you actually need by a date.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is AliExpress available in Pakistan?


Yes. The site and app work in Pakistan, Pakistan is a delivery destination, and most sellers ship here. Payment is prepaid, delivery takes weeks, and duty may be collected on arrival.


### Is AliExpress banned or blocked in Pakistan?


No. There is no block, and you do not need a VPN — using one can actually get your card payment declined.


### Can I pay cash on delivery on AliExpress in Pakistan?


No. AliExpress is prepaid. For Chinese products with cash on delivery in rupees, Markaz China is the route Pakistani buyers use instead.


### Why does my card keep getting declined on AliExpress?


Most often the card is not enabled for international transactions, or the OTP was not completed. Enable international use in your banking app, keep your registered number reachable, and turn off any VPN before paying.


### How long does an AliExpress order take to reach Pakistan?


Weeks, and the range is wide — the shipping method you choose at checkout matters more than anything else. Economy shipping is the slowest lane; paid courier options move faster and track better.


### Will I have to pay customs duty on an AliExpress order?


You can. A cross-border parcel may be assessed on arrival and the courier typically collects before delivering. Treat the sticker price as a floor, not the landed cost.


### Can I return an AliExpress order from Pakistan?


You can open a dispute inside the buyer-protection window shown on your order page. A physical return goes back to China at your cost, which often exceeds the item's value, so a partial refund is usually the practical outcome.


### Does AliExpress deliver to smaller cities in Pakistan?


Delivery depends on the courier handling the last mile, and coverage is wider in the big cities. Give a landmark and a number that will be answered — an unreachable phone is the most common reason a cross-border parcel sits at a depot.


### Is AliExpress cheaper than buying in Pakistan?


On the listing page, often. After shipping, currency conversion and anything collected at the door, the gap narrows and sometimes closes. Compare landed cost against a local price before you decide.
